# Technology stack

This document records the technologies, direct third-party dependencies, development tools, hosted services, and external data sources currently selected for the Sport Analytics Tool.

The purpose is to make the project reproducible and auditable. `package.json` files define the direct JavaScript dependencies selected by the team, while `package-lock.json` is the authoritative record of the exact versions installed by `npm ci`.

## Stack boundaries

The project deliberately keeps the product applications separate:

```text
React frontend
    |
    | HTTPS requests to the handwritten API
    v
Express backend API
    |
    +--> Supabase Auth for managed identity verification
    |
    +--> PostgreSQL for application data
```

The frontend may communicate directly with Supabase Auth for managed sign-in and session handling. Application-domain data must pass through the handwritten Express API; generated Supabase Data API endpoints are not used as the application API.

## Languages and runtimes

| Technology           | Project version / requirement             | Purpose                                                                     | Motivation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript           | `5.5.4`                                   | Primary application language across frontend, backend and shared contracts. | One typed language across all workspaces allows schemas and types to be shared, catches interface errors before runtime, and fits the Node.js/React ecosystem already selected. It is pinned because the current `@typescript-eslint` version supports TypeScript below 5.6. |
| JavaScript / Node.js | Node.js `>=20`; Azure uses Node.js 22 LTS | Executes build tooling and the backend runtime.                             | Keeps the backend in the same ecosystem as the TypeScript frontend and is supported by the selected Azure App Service deployment.                                                                                                                                            |
| Python               | Project baseline: Python `>=3.10`         | Builds the MkDocs documentation and runs the Cricsheet acquisition script.  | Python is used only for documentation/data-support tasks; the product applications remain TypeScript/Node.js. The Cricsheet downloader uses only the Python standard library.                                                                                                |
| SQL                  | PostgreSQL SQL                            | Defines migrations, constraints and database queries.                       | Plain SQL keeps schema changes explicit, reviewable and portable between PostgreSQL hosts.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## Frontend

| Technology / dependency      | Declared version | Purpose                                               | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| React                        | `^18.3.1`        | Component-based web user interface.                   | Selected in the initial scaffold for a non-monolithic frontend. No formal framework comparison is currently recorded.                                               |
| React DOM                    | `^18.3.1`        | Renders React components in the browser.              | Required runtime companion to React for the web application.                                                                                                        |
| React Router DOM             | `^7.18.2`        | Client-side routing and navigation.                   | Provides route matching and navigation without coupling routing logic to individual components.                                                                     |
| Vite                         | `^5.4.10`        | Development server and production frontend build.     | Provides a fast local development loop and a static production bundle suitable for the selected deployment model.                                                   |
| `@vitejs/plugin-react`       | `^4.3.3`         | React support in Vite.                                | Connects the selected React frontend to the Vite build pipeline.                                                                                                    |
| `@supabase/supabase-js`      | `^2.112.1`       | Managed browser authentication and session handling.  | Reuses the selected Supabase Auth platform rather than implementing authentication. Application data still uses the handwritten API.                                |
| `@sport-analytics/contracts` | `0.1.0`          | Shared request/response schemas and TypeScript types. | Prevents the frontend and backend from independently redefining the same contracts. Its exact version matches the local workspace package, as enforced by syncpack. |

## Backend API

| Technology / dependency      | Declared version | Purpose                                                         | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Express                      | `^4.21.1`        | Handwritten HTTP API, routing and middleware.                   | Satisfies the requirement for a separately implemented backend and handwritten API. No formal backend-framework comparison is currently recorded. |
| `@supabase/supabase-js`      | `^2.112.1`       | Validates Supabase access tokens on protected backend requests. | Uses the same managed identity platform as the frontend without trusting browser-only claims.                                                     |
| `pg`                         | `^8.22.0`        | PostgreSQL driver and connection pooling.                       | Keeps database access provider-neutral and communicates with PostgreSQL directly instead of generated Supabase data endpoints.                    |
| Zod                          | `^3.23.8`        | Runtime validation and schema-derived TypeScript types.         | Shared validation at the API boundary reduces drift between declared types and runtime payload validation.                                        |
| CORS                         | `^2.8.5`         | Cross-origin request policy.                                    | Explicitly limits which browser origins may call the API.                                                                                         |
| Helmet                       | `^8.0.0`         | Secure HTTP response-header defaults.                           | Adds established defensive HTTP headers instead of reimplementing them manually.                                                                  |
| Pino HTTP                    | `^10.3.0`        | Structured HTTP request logging.                                | Produces machine-readable request logs and supports redaction of sensitive headers such as `Authorization`.                                       |
| dotenv                       | `^17.4.2`        | Loads ignored local backend environment files.                  | Keeps local configuration outside committed source while preserving a simple developer setup.                                                     |
| `@sport-analytics/contracts` | `0.1.0`          | Shared API schemas/types.                                       | Keeps backend responses and validation aligned with the shared contract boundary.                                                                 |

## Shared contracts

| Technology / dependency | Declared version    | Purpose                                         | Motivation / notes                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Zod                     | `^3.23.8`           | Runtime schemas and TypeScript type derivation. | Allows the same contract definition to be consumed by frontend, backend and tests without storing business logic in the package. |
| TypeScript              | inherited from root | Builds the package and emits declarations.      | Makes the contracts package usable as a typed workspace dependency.                                                              |

## Database and authentication services

| Technology / service      | Current selection                                           | Purpose                                                                                        | Motivation and alternatives                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PostgreSQL                | Supabase-hosted PostgreSQL                                  | Persistent application data, event provenance, accounts, scopes and future derived statistics. | ADR-003 selected PostgreSQL on Supabase for provisioning speed and team familiarity while preserving a standard connection-string boundary. Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Neon were considered as hosting alternatives. |
| Supabase database hosting | Paid-plan Supabase project; session pooler on port 5432     | Hosts PostgreSQL with enough capacity for the planned event dataset.                           | The project moved away from the storage-constrained original project. The Data API is disabled so generated data endpoints are not available. ADR-005 records the migration decision and its alternatives.                  |
| Supabase Auth             | Managed Supabase Auth; Google is the initial OAuth provider | Sign-up/sign-in lifecycle, OAuth, sessions and token issuance.                                 | ADR-004 selected Supabase Auth after Firebase was superseded, avoiding a second identity platform while preserving the handwritten API boundary. Auth0 and custom authentication were also considered.                      |
| Supavisor session pooler  | Port 5432                                                   | Reliable PostgreSQL connectivity from developer machines and deployment environments.          | ADR-003 rejected the direct connection because IPv4 could not be assumed and rejected transaction-mode pooling because prepared statements are required.                                                                    |
| `node-pg-migrate`         | `^9.0.0`                                                    | Applies ordered SQL migrations.                                                                | ADR-003 selected explicit SQL migrations and rejected Drizzle Kit at this stage because it would introduce a schema-generation/ORM direction that had not been chosen.                                                      |

ADR-005 records the database host and authentication service as separate Supabase project concerns at the time of that decision. If the team later consolidates them into one project or changes account ownership/tier, that change must be recorded separately rather than silently rewriting the historical ADR.

## Testing and verification

| Technology / dependency     | Declared version                             | Purpose                                                                  | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Vitest                      | `^2.1.4`                                     | Frontend, backend and contract unit/integration tests.                   | One test runner across TypeScript workspaces reduces duplicated configuration.                                                                                        |
| `embedded-postgres`         | `^16.14.0-beta.17`                           | Default disposable PostgreSQL 16 integration-test runtime.               | Runs the real database integration suite on demand without Docker, administrator rights, or a hosted test database.                                                   |
| Docker / Docker Compose     | Docker Desktop or compatible Compose runtime | Provisions the disposable local PostgreSQL integration-test environment. | Gives each developer an isolated, reproducible database without a hosted test project or shared credentials while keeping normal development independent from Docker. |
| PostgreSQL container image  | `postgres:16`                                | Runs the repository-managed local integration-test database.             | Uses the same PostgreSQL major version as CI so local database behaviour closely matches the automated pipeline.                                                      |
| React Testing Library       | `^16.0.1`                                    | React component behaviour tests.                                         | Encourages testing through user-observable component behaviour rather than implementation details.                                                                    |
| `@testing-library/jest-dom` | `^6.6.3`                                     | DOM-specific assertions.                                                 | Improves readability of frontend tests.                                                                                                                               |
| jsdom                       | `^25.0.1`                                    | Browser-like DOM environment for Vitest.                                 | Allows React tests to run without launching a full browser.                                                                                                           |
| Supertest                   | `^7.0.0`                                     | HTTP assertions against the Express application.                         | Exercises API behaviour through HTTP without requiring a separately deployed server.                                                                                  |
| Playwright                  | `@playwright/test ^1.62.1`                   | Browser end-to-end testing.                                              | Verifies actual navigation and user flows in a real browser engine.                                                                                                   |
| `@axe-core/playwright`      | `^4.12.1`                                    | Automated accessibility checks.                                          | Integrates the compatible axe-core engine with Playwright for repeatable detection of serious accessibility violations in browser-level verification.                 |
| `@vitest/coverage-v8`       | `^2.1.9`                                     | Test coverage reporting.                                                 | Uses V8 coverage with the existing Vitest test runner.                                                                                                                |

## Code quality and build tooling

| Technology / dependency            | Declared version         | Purpose                                                                     | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ESLint                             | `^8.57.1`                | Static linting.                                                             | Enforces shared code-quality rules before review.                                                                                                        |
| `@typescript-eslint/parser`        | `^7.18.0`                | Parses TypeScript for ESLint.                                               | Required for TypeScript-aware linting.                                                                                                                   |
| `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` | `^7.18.0`                | TypeScript lint rules.                                                      | Extends ESLint with TypeScript-specific checks.                                                                                                          |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`        | `^4.6.2`                 | React Hooks lint rules.                                                     | Detects invalid Hook usage and missing dependency patterns.                                                                                              |
| Prettier                           | `^3.3.3`                 | Repository formatting.                                                      | Gives the team one deterministic formatting command and avoids style-only review debates.                                                                |
| `.editorconfig`                    | repository configuration | Basic editor-independent whitespace/line-ending rules.                      | Keeps common formatting behaviour consistent even when team members use different editors.                                                               |
| `cross-env`                        | `^10.1.0`                | Cross-platform environment variables in npm scripts.                        | Keeps database/test scripts usable on Windows and Unix-like systems.                                                                                     |
| `tsx`                              | `^4.19.2`                | Executes TypeScript backend development and support scripts directly.       | Avoids a separate manual compile step for local scripts and watch mode.                                                                                  |
| npm workspaces                     | npm `>=10`               | Monorepo dependency and script orchestration.                               | Allows frontend, backend and contracts to share one lock file while remaining separate packages.                                                         |
| Knip                               | `^6.32.2`                | Detects unused files, dependencies, exports and types.                      | Finds monorepo maintenance issues that ordinary builds, tests and lint rules do not expose.                                                              |
| syncpack                           | `^15.3.3`                | Validates dependency-version consistency across npm workspaces.             | Prevents package-version drift as contributors change frontend, backend and shared dependencies.                                                         |
| dependency-cruiser                 | `^18.2.0`                | Validates the monorepo source dependency graph and architecture boundaries. | Automates circular-dependency detection and the documented frontend/backend/contracts boundaries rather than relying only on manual Pull Request review. |

## API documentation tooling

| Technology / dependency | Declared version        | Purpose                               | Motivation / notes                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| OpenAPI                 | `docs/api/openapi.yaml` | Machine-readable public API contract. | Gives API consumers a version-controlled specification independent of implementation code. |
| Redocly CLI             | `^2.46.0`               | Lints the OpenAPI specification.      | Makes API contract validation part of `npm run check`.                                     |

## Documentation tooling

| Technology / dependency | Version / requirement                            | Purpose                                                       | Motivation / alternatives                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MkDocs                  | installed through `mkdocs-material` requirements | Builds the public documentation site from Markdown.           | Keeps documentation version-controlled alongside the code. Docusaurus and mdBook were course-suggested alternatives; no formal comparison is currently recorded.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Material for MkDocs     | `>=9,<10`                                        | Documentation theme, navigation and search integration.       | Adds a readable documentation UI without requiring the team to build a docs frontend.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Cloudflare Pages        | hosted service                                   | Publicly hosts the generated MkDocs `site/` output.           | Already deployed and independently accessible; avoids an account-gated documentation platform.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Wrangler                | `^4.119.0`                                       | Deploys the generated documentation site to Cloudflare Pages. | Provides a repeatable CLI deployment command suitable for local use and future automation. Because it is invoked through the documented `npx wrangler` command rather than imported by source, the root Knip workspace has a dependency-specific exception for it. Wrangler is not used to deploy the React frontend or Express backend. |

## Deployment, collaboration and CI/CD

| Technology / service          | Purpose                                                                  | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Git                           | Version control.                                                         | Required project history and traceability mechanism.                                                                                                                     |
| Gitea                         | Repository hosting, issues, Pull Requests, project board and milestones. | University-hosted collaboration platform used as the authoritative project record.                                                                                       |
| GitHub Flow adapted for Gitea | Branch/PR methodology.                                                   | Selected over Git Flow to keep review and traceability without permanent `develop`/release branches. See `docs/git-methodology.md`.                                      |
| Gitea Actions                 | Continuous integration and Azure deployment workflows.                   | Keeps automated checks and deployment definitions in the same repository.                                                                                                |
| Azure App Service (Linux)     | Hosts the React frontend and Express backend.                            | ADR 0003 selected App Service for managed HTTPS, Node.js support and a simple Sprint 1 deployment model. Azure Container Apps and Azure Static Web Apps were considered. |
| Cloudflare Pages              | Hosts public documentation.                                              | Keeps the documentation deployment independent from the application deployments.                                                                                         |

## External data and integrations

| Source / service | Current use                                       | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Cricsheet        | Historical event-level T20/IT20 JSON data source. | Downloaded by `scripts/download_cricsheet_t20.py`; generated bulk data remains ignored. Cricsheet is a historical file/data source rather than the course-required runtime external API integration.                           |
| Google OAuth     | Identity provider through Supabase Auth.          | Provides the initial managed OAuth sign-in path. OAuth client secrets remain in provider dashboards and are never committed.                                                                                                   |
| Open-Meteo       | Runtime external weather API integration.         | Selected in ADR-008 and called server-side by the Express backend through `GET /api/v1/weather`. It requires no API key. Provider failures are isolated to the weather feature through validation, timeout and error handling. |

## Type-only support packages

The following direct packages provide TypeScript declarations for JavaScript libraries or runtimes. They do not add separate runtime behaviour:

- `@types/react ^18.3.12`
- `@types/react-dom ^18.3.1`
- `@types/cors ^2.8.17`
- `@types/express ^4.17.21`
- `@types/node ^22.9.0`
- `@types/pg ^8.20.4`
- `@types/supertest ^6.0.2`

## Version policy

- `package-lock.json` is committed and defines the exact JavaScript dependency graph used by `npm ci`.
- Developers must use `npm ci` for clean-clone verification and CI-equivalent checks.
- Direct dependencies must not be added without a clear project purpose.
- Significant technology changes require a Gitea issue and, where they affect architecture, a decision record.
- New third-party code/services must be added to this document and to the relevant specialist documentation.
- Dependency upgrades must be tested before merge.

## Editor and operating-system policy

No IDE or operating system is required by the repository. The setup guide provides Windows PowerShell and Unix-like command equivalents where the command differs. Team members should record the OS, terminal/shell, editor/IDE and exact tool versions used during onboarding verification so the team can identify environment-specific problems without making one editor a project dependency.

## AI tooling

AI usage is governed separately by the course AI policy and the repository AI evidence process. The root README records the repository-level AI code-generation, inline-editing and code-review declarations, while task-level tool/model/purpose records and transcripts are stored under `evidence/ai/`.

# Technology stack

This document records the technologies, direct third-party dependencies, development tools, hosted services, and external data sources currently selected for the Sport Analytics Tool.

The purpose is to make the project reproducible and auditable. `package.json` files define the direct JavaScript dependencies selected by the team, while `package-lock.json` is the authoritative record of the exact versions installed by `npm ci`.

## Stack boundaries

The project deliberately keeps the product applications separate:

```text
React frontend
    |
    | HTTPS requests to the handwritten API
    v
Express backend API
    |
    +--> Supabase Auth for managed identity verification
    |
    +--> PostgreSQL for application data
```

The frontend may communicate directly with Supabase Auth for managed sign-in and session handling. Application-domain data must pass through the handwritten Express API; generated Supabase Data API endpoints are not used as the application API.

## Languages and runtimes

| Technology           | Project version / requirement             | Purpose                                                                     | Motivation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript           | `5.5.4`                                   | Primary application language across frontend, backend and shared contracts. | One typed language across all workspaces allows schemas and types to be shared, catches interface errors before runtime, and fits the Node.js/React ecosystem already selected. It is pinned because the current `@typescript-eslint` version supports TypeScript below 5.6. |
| JavaScript / Node.js | Node.js `>=20`; Azure uses Node.js 22 LTS | Executes build tooling and the backend runtime.                             | Keeps the backend in the same ecosystem as the TypeScript frontend and is supported by the selected Azure App Service deployment.                                                                                                                                            |
| Python               | Project baseline: Python `>=3.10`         | Builds the MkDocs documentation and runs the Cricsheet acquisition script.  | Python is used only for documentation/data-support tasks; the product applications remain TypeScript/Node.js. The Cricsheet downloader uses only the Python standard library.                                                                                                |
| SQL                  | PostgreSQL SQL                            | Defines migrations, constraints and database queries.                       | Plain SQL keeps schema changes explicit, reviewable and portable between PostgreSQL hosts.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## Frontend

| Technology / dependency      | Declared version | Purpose                                               | Motivation / notes                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| React                        | `^18.3.1`        | Component-based web user interface.                   | Selected in the initial scaffold for a non-monolithic frontend. No formal framework comparison is currently recorded.                                               |
| React DOM                    | `^18.3.1`        | Renders React components in the browser.              | Required runtime companion to React for the web application.                                                                                                        |
| React Router DOM             | `^7.18.2`        | Client-side routing and navigation.                   | Provides route matching and navigation without coupling routing logic to individual components.                                                                     |
| Vite                         | `^5.4.10`        | Development server and production frontend build.     | Provides a fast local development loop and a static production bundle suitable for the selected deployment model.                                                   |
| `@vitejs/plugin-react`       | `^4.3.3`         | React support in Vite.                                | Connects the selected React frontend to the Vite build pipeline.                                                                                                    |
| `@supabase/supabase-js`      | `^2.112.1`       | Managed browser authentication and session handling.  | Reuses the selected Supabase Auth platform rather than implementing authentication. Application data still uses the handwritten API.                                |
| `@sport-analytics/contracts` | `0.1.0`          | Shared request/response schemas and TypeScript types. | Prevents the frontend and backend from independently redefining the same contracts. Its exact version matches the local workspace package, as enforced by syncpack. |

| `@supabase/supabase-js`      | `^2.112.1`       | Validates Supabase access tokens on protected backend requests. | Uses the same managed identity platform as the frontend without trusting browser-only claims.                                                     |

## Database and authentication services

| Technology / service      | Current selection                                           | Purpose                                                                                        | Motivation and alternatives                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PostgreSQL                | Supabase-hosted PostgreSQL                                  | Persistent application data, event provenance, accounts, scopes and future derived statistics. | ADR-003 selected PostgreSQL on Supabase for provisioning speed and team familiarity while preserving a standard connection-string boundary. Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Neon were considered as hosting alternatives. |
| Supabase database hosting | Paid-plan Supabase project; session pooler on port 5432     | Hosts PostgreSQL with enough capacity for the planned event dataset.                           | The project moved away from the storage-constrained original project. The Data API is disabled so generated data endpoints are not available. ADR-005 records the migration decision and its alternatives.                  |
| Supabase Auth             | Managed Supabase Auth; Google is the initial OAuth provider | Sign-up/sign-in lifecycle, OAuth, sessions and token issuance.                                 | ADR-004 selected Supabase Auth after Firebase was superseded, avoiding a second identity platform while preserving the handwritten API boundary. Auth0 and custom authentication were also considered.                      |
| Supavisor session pooler  | Port 5432                                                   | Reliable PostgreSQL connectivity from developer machines and deployment environments.          | ADR-003 rejected the direct connection because IPv4 could not be assumed and rejected transaction-mode pooling because prepared statements are required.                                                                    |
| `node-pg-migrate`         | `^9.0.0`                                                    | Applies ordered SQL migrations.                                                                | ADR-003 selected explicit SQL migrations and rejected Drizzle Kit at this stage because it would introduce a schema-generation/ORM direction that had not been chosen.                                                      |

ADR-005 records the database host and authentication service as separate Supabase project concerns at the time of that decision. If the team later consolidates them into one project or changes account ownership/tier, that change must be recorded separately rather than silently rewriting the historical ADR.

- `package-lock.json` is committed and defines the exact JavaScript dependency graph used by `npm ci`.

- New third-party code/services must be added to this document and to the relevant specialist documentation.
- Dependency upgrades must be tested before merge.

## Related public detail-overview coverage

The competition, season, and team detail-page suites verify readable related seasons, fixtures,
teams, and players; season-grouped competition fixtures; direct fixture-overview links; fixture-first
season content; independent loading, empty, error, retry, and cursor-pagination states; and the
absence of visible technical identifiers and backend resource terminology. The public-browsing
browser suite follows the competition-to-season-to-fixture journey in three keyboard activations,
visits the team overview, checks desktop and mobile overflow, and scans the result for serious or
critical Axe findings.

Run the focused checks with:

```text
npm run test --workspace=@sport-analytics/frontend -- --run src/pages/PublicBrowsePages.test.tsx
npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/public-browsing.spec.ts --workers=1
```

## Connected public-data journey coverage

The issue #199 browser verification treats the completed competition, season, fixture, team,
player, statistics, and calculation-trace redesign as connected tasks. The public-browsing journey
starts at Competitions and reaches a season and complete fixture overview in three keyboard
activations, then starts at Teams and reaches the same inline statistics in two. The player journey
starts at Players and reaches the player overview, named match, inline statistics, and calculation
trace in three keyboard activations.

Both journeys run in desktop and Pixel 7 Chromium. Day Match and Night Match are selected and
checked independently; each representative view is audited for readable headings, labels, facts,
filters, links, and messages, horizontal overflow, and serious or critical Axe findings. The
interaction matrix, command results, screenshot index, usability walkthrough, and deliberately
deferred follow-up are recorded in `evidence/validation/issue-199-public-data-journeys.md`.

Run the focused checks with:

```text
npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/public-browsing.spec.ts tests/e2e/player-overview.spec.ts --workers=1
```

# Technology stack

This document records the technologies, direct third-party dependencies, development tools, hosted services, and external data sources currently selected for the Sport Analytics Tool.

The purpose is to make the project reproducible and auditable. `package.json` files define the direct JavaScript dependencies selected by the team, while `package-lock.json` is the authoritative record of the exact versions installed by `npm ci`.

## Stack boundaries

The project deliberately keeps the product applications separate:

```text
React frontend
    |
    | HTTPS requests to the handwritten API
    v
Express backend API
    |
    +--> Supabase Auth for managed identity verification
    |
    +--> PostgreSQL for application data
```

The frontend may communicate directly with Supabase Auth for managed sign-in and session handling. Application-domain data must pass through the handwritten Express API; generated Supabase Data API endpoints are not used as the application API.

# Technology stack

This document records the technologies, direct third-party dependencies, development tools, hosted services, and external data sources currently selected for the Sport Analytics Tool.

The purpose is to make the project reproducible and auditable. `package.json` files define the direct JavaScript dependencies selected by the team, while `package-lock.json` is the authoritative record of the exact versions installed by `npm ci`.

## Stack boundaries

The project deliberately keeps the product applications separate:

```text
React frontend

Express backend API

    +--> Supabase Auth for managed identity verification
    |
    +--> PostgreSQL for application data

﻿# Nadav Sundy - Local Codex Instructions
# Sport Analytics Tool

These instructions apply only to Nadav Sundy's local development workflow.

## Core rule

Implement exactly the supplied Gitea issue.

The issue description and acceptance criteria define the scope.

Do not add features, refactors, cleanup, architectural changes, dependency
upgrades, documentation rewrites, or other improvements unless they are
directly necessary to satisfy the issue's acceptance criteria or an explicit
project requirement that applies to the change.

If useful work is discovered outside the issue scope, report it as proposed
follow-up work. Do not implement it.

If an out-of-scope change appears necessary to complete the issue, stop and
explain why before making that change.

## Before implementation

Before changing files:

1. Inspect:
   - git status
   - current branch
   - recent relevant history

2. Confirm that the supplied issue has:
   - a clear description;
   - acceptance criteria;
   - enough information to determine what "done" means.

If only an issue number is supplied and its contents are not available, do not
guess the requirements. Ask for the issue contents.

3. Read the project rules before planning implementation:
   - README.md
   - docs/git-methodology.md
   - docs/project_methodology.md
   - docs/ai/usage.md
   - evidence/ai/registers/README.md

The per-member register rules in evidence/ai/registers/README.md are the
current workflow for AI usage records. Nadav's register is:

evidence/ai/registers/nadav-sundy.csv

Do not record Nadav's usage in another team member's file.

4. Read documentation relevant to the affected area before modifying it.

Examples:
- frontend/UI -> docs/design/, docs/architecture/
- backend/API -> docs/api/, docs/architecture/
- database -> docs/database/, relevant ADRs
- authentication/security -> docs/security/, relevant ADRs
- data pipeline -> docs/data/
- deployment/CI -> docs/deployment/
- testing -> docs/development/testing.md
- significant architecture decisions -> docs/adr/

Do not assume existing architecture or conventions from memory when repository
documentation defines them.

## Git workflow

Follow docs/git-methodology.md exactly.

Never develop directly on main.

Before starting a new issue, main must be current.

A development branch must follow:

<type>/<issue-number>-<short-description>

Use only the approved branch types from docs/git-methodology.md.

A branch should address one issue.

Every normal development commit must reference the issue using:

Refs #<issue-number>

Do not push, merge, close an issue, or create/merge a Pull Request unless Nadav
explicitly asks for that action.

Never force-push main.

## Scope control

Before editing a file, be able to explain how that file contributes to an
acceptance criterion or an applicable Definition of Done requirement.

Prefer the smallest correct change.

Do not:
- perform opportunistic refactoring;
- rename unrelated code;
- reformat unrelated files;
- upgrade dependencies unless required;
- change public interfaces unnecessarily;
- change database schemas unless required;
- introduce new frameworks or libraries when the existing project approach is
  sufficient;
- implement future backlog items;
- implement adjacent features because they would be convenient;
- delete apparently unused code without proving that removal is required;
- weaken tests to make an implementation pass.

Preserve backwards compatibility where the issue does not explicitly require a
breaking change.

## Architecture

Respect all documented repository boundaries.

In particular, do not bypass the handwritten backend HTTP API for application
data.

Do not introduce an alternative authentication architecture, generated
application-data API, second backend, or conflicting technology where project
documentation has already selected an approach.

If the requested implementation conflicts with an approved ADR, architecture
document, security decision, or database design, stop and report the conflict.

## Implementation

First inspect existing code and tests for the established pattern.

Use existing abstractions where they fit.

Keep the implementation understandable and as small as reasonably possible.

Handle errors required by the issue and established project conventions.

Do not invent requirements.

Do not silently change behaviour outside the requested feature.

## Testing

Behavioural changes require relevant tests.

Use the repository's existing test framework and conventions.

Determine test, lint, formatting, build and type-check commands from repository
configuration and documentation. Do not invent commands.

Run the narrowest useful tests during development, then run all applicable
checks required by the project before declaring the issue complete.

Never claim a test passed unless the command was actually executed and exited
successfully.

Never disable, skip, delete or weaken an existing test merely to make the
implementation pass.

If an applicable check cannot be run, state exactly why.

## Documentation

Update documentation only where required because behaviour, setup, API
contracts, database schema, security behaviour, deployment, or another
documented interface changed.

Do not rewrite unrelated documentation.

For AI-assisted written documents, follow docs/ai/usage.md and the course AI
policy for document declarations.

## AI attribution

Codex is AI code generation.

Any commit containing code generated or materially modified by this Codex
session must contain:

Assisted-by: Codex[ACTUAL MODEL USED -- for the current session shown as gpt-5.6-sol, write GPT-5.6 Sol]

Use the exact model actually used by the session.

Never guess, approximate, reuse a model name from an old commit, or assume the
model from README.md.

If the exact model cannot be established, stop before committing and ask Nadav.

Only AI tools genuinely involved in the contents of that commit may appear in
its Assisted-by trailers.

If another AI tool also materially generated code in the same commit, include
that tool and its real model as required by the course policy.

## Nadav's AI usage register

For material Codex work retained in the project, update only:

evidence/ai/registers/nadav-sundy.csv

Follow evidence/ai/registers/README.md exactly.

Requirements include:
- every field quoted;
- dates use YYYY-MM-DD;
- semicolons rather than commas for multiple items inside a field;
- preserve the header;
- preserve valid CSV;
- file ends with a trailing newline;
- list only tools and models actually used;
- do not invent transcript paths, Pull Requests, commits or verification.

The Tool value for this CLI is Codex.

The Model value must be the exact active model.

The Brief task should identify the issue where applicable.

The Output used field must describe only output actually retained.

The Verification or adaptation field may state objective checks actually
performed, such as specific tests, linting or type-checking.

Do not claim that Nadav personally reviewed, understood, verified or adapted AI
output unless Nadav explicitly confirms that this happened.

If human verification is still pending, say so rather than claiming
verification.

Do not edit another team member's AI register.

## Commit messages

Follow the simplified Conventional Commit format defined in
docs/git-methodology.md.

Use:

<type>(<scope>): <imperative description>

or:

<type>: <imperative description>

A code-generation commit should therefore normally resemble:

<type>(<scope>): <description>

Refs #<issue-number>
Assisted-by: Codex[ACTUAL MODEL USED -- for the current session shown as gpt-5.6-sol, write GPT-5.6 Sol]

Do not create vague messages such as "changes", "fix stuff", "updates" or
"final".

Keep commits logically focused.

## Completion check

Before saying the issue is complete:

1. Re-read the issue and every acceptance criterion.
2. Inspect git diff.
3. Identify every changed file and why it was necessary.
4. Confirm there are no unrelated changes.
5. Run applicable tests and quality checks.
6. Confirm required documentation was updated and unrelated documentation was
   untouched.
7. Confirm architecture and project methodology remain compliant.
8. Confirm AI attribution requirements have been handled.
9. Confirm Nadav's AI register is valid if it was updated.
10. Report:
    - acceptance criteria satisfied;
    - files changed;
    - tests/checks run and results;
    - documentation changed;
    - any limitations;
    - any suggested follow-up work that was deliberately NOT implemented.

Do not describe an issue as complete if an acceptance criterion is unresolved.


## Completion terminology

Distinguish between implementation completion and project Definition of Done.

When all work that can be completed locally has been implemented and verified,
but the Pull Request has not yet been reviewed, merged and the Gitea issue has
not yet been closed, describe the state as:

"Implementation ready for review"

Do not describe the Gitea issue itself as "Done" or "complete" until the
repository's formal Definition of Done has actually been satisfied.

At the end of local implementation, clearly state which Definition of Done
steps remain, such as:
- human review;
- Pull Request creation;
- peer approval;
- merge into main;
- issue closure.

Do not perform those actions unless Nadav explicitly requests them.

content.text:
Implementation ready for review.

## Summary

Redesigned the public homepage into an editorial, cricket-broadcast-inspired landing page featuring:

- Approved “The game, measured ball by ball.” headline and public browsing routes.
- Explosive / Exact / Traceable brand narrative.
- A semantic delivery → derived statistic → source example using supported fields.
- Fixtures, Competitions, Players, and Teams navigation.
- Existing public API endpoints presented as part of the product identity.
- Responsive Day Match and Night Match presentations.
- A static SVG hero enhanced by one lazy-loaded procedural Three.js scene.

No commit was created.

## Key design decisions

- Preserved the approved logo and existing semantic colour tokens.
- Added self-hosted Latin subsets of Barlow Condensed, IBM Plex Sans, and IBM Plex Mono.
- Clearly labels the delivery path as illustrative—not real tracking data.
- Keeps all homepage content static; no application-data requests were introduced.
- Uses an editorial layout rather than generic feature cards.
- Mobile deliberately stacks and simplifies the hero presentation.

## Changed files

Implementation:

- [App.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/App.tsx>)
- [main.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/main.tsx>)
- [styles.css](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/styles.css>)
- [HomePage.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/features/home/HomePage.tsx>) and the new `features/home` components
- [frontend package.json](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/package.json>)
- [package-lock.json](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/package-lock.json>)

Tests:

- [HomePage.test.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/features/home/HomePage.test.tsx>)
- [App.test.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/App.test.tsx>)
- [homepage.spec.ts](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/tests/e2e/homepage.spec.ts>)
- [smoke.spec.ts](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts>)

Documentation and policy:

- [frontend README](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/README.md>)
- [features README](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/features/README.md>)
- [information architecture](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/docs/design/information-architecture-and-wireframes.md>)
- [testing documentation](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/docs/development/testing.md>)
- [technology stack](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/docs/development/technology-stack.md>)
- [Nadav’s AI register](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/evidence/ai/registers/nadav-sundy.csv>)

## Three.js and performance

- Three.js is dynamically imported after the semantic fallback renders.
- One procedural canvas; no models, textures, shadows, HDR, or post-processing.
- Device pixel ratio is capped at 1.5.
- Animation pauses off-screen, while the tab is hidden, and under reduced motion.
- RAF loops, timers, observers, listeners, geometries, materials, renderer, and WebGL context are cleaned up.
- Theme colours update while the scene remains mounted.
- Production build emitted Three.js as a separate `HeroScene` chunk: 527.90 kB raw / 133.65 kB gzip.
- The build retains Vite’s warning for chunks above 500 kB, but Three.js is excluded from the critical initial chunk.

## Accessibility and reduced motion

- One meaningful H1 and semantic heading hierarchy.
- Essential content remains HTML; the canvas is `aria-hidden`.
- Native links, visible focus, keyboard navigation, and mobile touch targets are preserved.
- Reduced motion prevents Three.js loading and stops fallback animation.
- WebGL and chunk failures leave the intentional SVG presentation visible.
- Day and Night themes passed serious/critical Axe checks.

## Verification

Passed:

- Targeted Prettier checks and `git diff --check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run typecheck`
- Focused Vitest: 18 tests
- `npm run test`: 383 database-independent tests
- `npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1`: 52 tests
- `npm run openapi:lint`
- `npm run build`
- `python -m mkdocs build --strict`
- `npm run hygiene:dependencies`
- `npm run hygiene:architecture`

Manually inspected Day desktop, Night desktop, and Pixel 7 mobile production screenshots.

Existing unrelated repository findings remain:

- `npm run check` stops on the pre-existing formatting issue in `AGENTS.override.md`.
- Knip reports the pre-existing unused `docs/javascripts/external-links.js` and backend `CorrectionTarget` export.
- `package-lock.json` already contained unrelated uncommitted npm metadata churn before this issue; it was preserved while adding the required dependencies.

## Scope and policy

No backend, database, schema, contract, authentication, or API implementation changes were made. No ball-location fields or data fetches were introduced.

Only Nadav’s AI register was updated, with Codex and the exact model `GPT-5.6 Sol`. Human review remains pending.

Remaining Definition of Done steps: human review, commit, Pull Request, peer approval, merge into `main`, and issue closure.

Proposed commit message:

```text
feat(frontend): redesign homepage with branded motion

Refs #314
Assisted-by: Codex[GPT-5.6 Sol]
```

Implementation ready for review. The runtime stability bug is fixed without changing the hero design.

## Root cause

In React development StrictMode, `HeroScene` followed this sequence:

1. Create renderer.
2. StrictMode cleanup called `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
3. StrictMode remounted the effect and created a new renderer on the same canvas.
4. The deferred context-loss event then reached that live canvas and invalidated the new renderer.

The reproduced console message was:

```text
THREE.WebGLRenderer: Context Lost.
```

It occurred approximately 1.58 seconds after loading. The mounted canvas subsequently retained `data-animation-state="disposed"`, explaining why the failure appeared after the hero initially worked.

The WebGL capability probe also unnecessarily invoked `WEBGL_lose_context`; that was removed.

## Fix

- Removed normal-cleanup `renderer.forceContextLoss()`.
- Cached the WebGL capability result without deliberately losing its probe context.
- Added per-effect `disposed` and `contextLost` guards.
- Ensured only one RAF and replay timer can be scheduled.
- Prevented RAF, observer, visibility, reduced-motion, theme, and restoration callbacks from rendering after cleanup starts.
- Cleanup now:
  - marks the instance disposed;
  - cancels RAF and timers;
  - disconnects observers;
  - removes all listeners;
  - disposes geometries and materials;
  - calls `renderer.dispose()` exactly once.
- Theme changes update existing materials without recreating the renderer.
- Added `webglcontextlost` handling that stops animation and immediately exposes the static fallback.
- Added `webglcontextrestored` handling that resumes the same scene, canvas, and renderer.
- Retained the guarded asynchronous Three.js import.

## Files changed for this fix

Implementation:

- [HeroScene.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/features/home/HeroScene.tsx>)
- [HomeHero.tsx](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/apps/frontend/src/features/home/HomeHero.tsx>)

- [nadav-sundy.csv](<C:/Users/nsund/Documents/SDP/Sport-Analytics-Tool/evidence/ai/registers/nadav-sundy.csv>)

## Verification

- Reproduced the original failure in development StrictMode with browser console and WebGL event instrumentation.
- Completed a 120.112-second development soak covering:
  - 12 Day/Night theme changes;
  - repeated off-screen/on-screen scrolling;
  - tab hiding/restoration;
  - navigation away and back;
  - desktop/mobile resizing.
- Soak results:
  - maximum canvases: 1;
  - maximum pending RAFs: 1;
  - context losses: 0;
  - console errors: 0;
  - page errors: 0;
  - every off-screen check paused correctly.
- Deliberately triggered `WEBGL_lose_context`:
  - fallback appeared;
  - failed canvas became invisible;
  - animation stopped;
  - restoration reused the original canvas;
  - no page errors occurred.
- Frontend lint: passed.

- Production build: passed; Three.js remains separately code-split.
- Targeted Prettier, `git diff --check`, strict MkDocs build, and AI-register validation: passed.

One headless Chromium diagnostic emitted generic software-renderer `ReadPixels` performance warnings; there were no Three.js context-loss errors or application exceptions.

No backend, API, database, dependency, or visual-design changes were made for this fix. No commit was created.
